name: an empty file is text, and renders as an empty page
a UTF-8 BOM is stripped before judging, so BOM + text is text
a multi-byte sequence cut off at the end of the window is text: the rest of it is simply not here yet
an ANSI-coloured log line is text: ESC (0x1b) is deliberately not a binary byte
tabs, newlines, form feeds and carriage returns are text
a lone NUL makes it binary
a zip header is binary: 0x08 is in the binary set, which is what catches archives early
UTF-16LE text is binary to us: every other byte is NUL, and we render UTF-8 only
invalid UTF-8 carrying no binary byte is still binary: a bare 0xff is not a code point
a lone 0x0b (vertical tab) makes it binary, per mimesniff, though 0x09 and 0x0c do not
0x1e (record separator) is binary: a file of ASCII separators is not something to read
